findings.evidence: Grep: `OrbitDerivative.lean:102 theorem realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt ... (Set.Ici t) t`, `OrbitDerivative.lean:141 theorem realOperator_differentiableWithinAt ... (Set.Ici t) t`, while the surrounding semigroup API uses the fixed natural domain `Basic.lean:423 theorem ... realOperator_continuousWithinAt ... (Set.Ici 0) t₀` and the roadmap asks for `t ↦ S(t)x` differentiable.
findings.fix: Prove the stronger API with `(Set.Ici 0)` at `t` (and derive the current right-neighborhood forms by monotonicity if still wanted), e.g. `HasDerivWithinAt (fun s => S.realOperator s (x : X)) ... (Set.Ici 0) t`.
findings.issue: `realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt`, `realOperator_differentiableWithinAt`, and `realOperator_derivWithin` use `(Set.Ici t)` as the differentiation set, so at `t > 0` they expose only a right derivative rather than the natural derivative of the orbit on its domain `[0,∞)`.

summary: The new derivative API is under-general: it proves only a moving right-neighborhood statement, not differentiability within the natural nonnegative-time domain.
